title: The CGRP–goblet cell axis
objective: Explain how nociceptor CGRP directs goblet cells via RAMP1.

steps.title: Neurons tell the lining to act
steps.body: Beyond immune cells, nociceptor **[[CGRP]]** acts on **[[goblet cell|goblet cells]]** — the mucus-secreting epithelial cells — through receptors containing **[[RAMP1]]**. So a sensory neuron can direct the gut's protective mucus layer. Yang et al. mapped this CGRP–RAMP1 axis.

steps.setup: You delete RAMP1 from goblet cells, then challenge the gut.
steps.prompt: What do you predict for the mucus/goblet response?
options: The CGRP-directed goblet response is lost, weakening that defense
Goblet cells respond even more strongly than they normally would
The neurons stop firing their action potentials altogether
Goblet cells respond as usual, since they make their own CGRP
steps.reveal: No receptor, no signal: deleting RAMP1 cuts the neuron→goblet instruction, so that arm of mucosal defense fails — clean evidence the axis is functional, using the receptor-removal logic from B6.

options: Remove the CGRP-directed goblet response entirely
Make the goblet cells respond even more strongly
Stop the neurons from firing their signals entirely
variants.explanation: Without the receptor, neuronal CGRP can't instruct the goblet cells.

steps.prompt: The CGRP–goblet axis shows neurons can signal to which partner, besides immune cells?
options: Epithelial cells of the gut lining
Smooth muscle cells of the gut wall
steps.explanation: Neurons direct epithelial (goblet) cells too — so the neuroimmune 'unit' really includes neurons, immune cells, and epithelium together.

variants.setup: CGRP from nerves acts on goblet cells.
variants.prompt: This adds which partner to the neuroimmune unit?
variants.reveal: Epithelial cells join neurons and immune cells in the gut unit.

sources.note: Nociceptors direct goblet cells via a CGRP-RAMP1 axis.
